i: "PPPs bring private efficiency to public projects."

h: Same chai shop in 200 cities. Same owner? No ☕
m: A business model where an owner lets others run outlets under its brand for a fee.
e: A tea chain lets local entrepreneurs open outlets with its brand, menu and training.
i: "Franchising helps a brand grow fast with others' investment."

h: That video looks real. It might not be 🎭
m: Fake videos or audio made with AI that look and sound like real people.
e: A fake video shows a celebrity promoting an investment scheme they never endorsed.
i: "Always check the source before believing or sharing a shocking video."

h: Out of every 100 sold, how many are yours? 🥧
m: The percentage of total sales in a market that one company has.
e: If 100 cars are sold and 40 are from one brand, that brand has 40% market share.
i: "Market share tells us how we are doing against competitors, not just last year."

h: Bought now, pay later. Here's the word for it 📑
m: Money a business owes its suppliers for things bought on credit.
e: A restaurant buys vegetables on credit and pays the vendor at month-end.
i: "Managing payables well helps keep enough cash in hand."

h: Read the JD twice. It tells you what they'll ask 📄
m: A document that lists a job's duties, skills needed and reporting line.
e: A JD for a marketing executive lists social media, campaign reports and 1 to 2 years' experience.
i: "I tailor my CV to the keywords in the job description."

h: ₹100 in India vs $1.2 in the US. Which buys more? 🍔
m: A way to compare countries' incomes based on what money can actually buy locally.
e: A haircut costs much less in India than in the US, so incomes go further here.
i: "By PPP, India is one of the world's largest economies."

h: Make money AND change lives? Yes, both 💚
m: A business that aims to solve a social problem while also earning profit.
e: A startup sells affordable sanitary pads made by rural women, creating jobs and health awareness.
i: "Social enterprises prove that purpose and profit can go together."

h: You've been chatting with a bot more than you think 💬
m: Software that talks with people through text or voice to answer questions.
e: A bank's WhatsApp chatbot tells you your balance and blocks your card any time.
i: "Chatbots handle routine questions, so staff can solve complex ones."

h: Small market. Loyal fans. Big profits? 🔍
m: A small, specific group of customers with special needs.
e: A brand that makes only left-handed notebooks serves a niche market.
i: "A niche lets a small brand beat big players by serving people better."

h: Your parents' favourite investment. Still smart? 🏦
m: Putting money in a bank for a fixed time at a fixed interest rate.
e: Grandpa keeps Rs 2 lakh in a 1-year FD at a fixed rate and gets interest at the end.
i: "FDs are safe and simple, but returns may barely beat inflation."

h: Sales this year, marketing next. Why companies do it 🔄
m: Moving employees between different roles to build wider skills.
e: A management trainee spends 3 months each in sales, finance and operations.
i: "Job rotation builds future leaders who understand the whole business."

h: AAA or junk? Companies get report cards too 🅰️
m: A grade from an agency showing how likely a company or country is to repay its debt.
e: A company rated AAA can borrow at lower interest than one rated BB.
i: "A rating downgrade makes borrowing costlier."

h: Your salary + your passion = this 💡
m: A small business or paid work done alongside a main job or studies.
e: A college student runs a small baking business on weekends.
i: "A side hustle builds real business skills early."

h: Ask AI better, get better answers ✍️
m: Writing clear, detailed instructions to get useful results from AI tools.
e: Instead of 'explain GST', a student writes 'explain GST to a class 10 student with one shop example'.
i: "Good prompts save time and give more accurate answers."

h: Why people now pay ₹300 for coffee instead of ₹20 ☕
m: When customers upgrade to more expensive, better-quality versions of products.
e: More Indian families now buy premium smartphones, cars and packaged foods than before.
i: "Premiumisation is a big opportunity as incomes rise."

h: Can't beat the market? Just buy the whole market 📊
m: A mutual fund that simply copies a market index like the Nifty 50.
e: A Nifty index fund holds all 50 Nifty companies in the same weights as the index.
i: "Index funds have low costs and suit long-term beginners."

h: Internship pay has a special name. Here it is 💵
m: A fixed amount paid to interns or trainees, usually lower than a salary.
e: An MBA intern gets a Rs 25,000 monthly stipend for a two-month summer internship.
i: "For internships, I value the learning more than the stipend."

h: Lend money to the government. Get paid interest 📜
m: A loan you give to a government or company, which pays you interest and returns the money later.
e: A government bond pays fixed interest every 6 months and returns the money after 10 years.
i: "Bonds are safer than shares but usually give lower returns."

h: Indians fix things with whatever they have. That's a skill 🔧
m: Finding clever, low-cost solutions with limited resources.
e: A farmer turns an old bike engine into a water pump for his field.
i: "Jugaad shows how constraints can spark creative solutions."

h: Why you can't break that 30-day streak 🔥
m: Using game features like points, badges and streaks in non-game apps.
e: A language app keeps you learning daily with streaks and leaderboards.
i: "Gamification makes boring habits feel rewarding."

h: When your new product eats your old one 🍽️
m: When a company's new product takes sales away from its own existing product.
e: A new cheaper phone model reduces sales of the same brand's older model.
i: "Some cannibalisation is fine if the company keeps the customer."

h: Borrowed money can make you rich. Or broke ⚠️
m: Using borrowed money to increase the size of an investment or business.
e: A trader uses Rs 10,000 of his own money and borrows Rs 90,000 to trade Rs 1 lakh of shares.
i: "Leverage multiplies both gains and losses, so it needs care."

h: The fastest way into a company? Someone inside 🤝
m: When an employee recommends someone they know for a job opening.
e: Amit refers his college friend for a role, and the company gives Amit a referral bonus.
i: "Referrals often bring good hires faster, so I build my network early."

h: When this number rises, loans get costlier 📈
m: The return an investor earns on a bond, as a percentage.
e: If a Rs 1,000 bond pays Rs 70 a year, its yield is 7%.
i: "Rising bond yields often push up loan rates in the economy."
tm: Fixed interest printed on the bond.

h: Slow, slow, slow… then BOOM 🏒
m: A growth pattern that stays flat for a while, then suddenly shoots up.
e: An app grows slowly for 2 years, then explodes after one feature goes viral.
i: "Most overnight successes had years of flat growth first."

h: Why some apps feel easy and others make you angry 😤
m: How easy and pleasant it is for someone to use a product or app.
e: A good payment app takes 3 taps, while a confusing one needs 10.
i: "Great UX reduces drop-offs and support calls."

h: Why the store sells this one item at a loss 🛒
m: A product sold very cheap, even at a loss, to bring customers in.
e: A supermarket sells sugar below cost, knowing shoppers will buy other items too.
i: "A loss leader works only if customers buy more profitable items with it."

h: Like insurance, but for investments 🛡️
m: Taking a position that reduces the risk of losing money on another investment.
e: An exporter fixes today's dollar rate for a payment due in 3 months, so a falling dollar won't hurt.
i: "Hedging reduces risk but also limits some upside."

h: When a company calls you for a job you never applied for 📞
m: Finding and approaching skilled people who are already employed elsewhere.
e: A recruiter calls a senior manager at a rival company with a better offer.
i: "Building a strong profile makes headhunters find you."

h: Small loans that changed millions of lives 💪
m: Small loans and financial services for poor people who don't have access to banks.
e: A woman in a village takes a Rs 20,000 loan to start a tailoring business.
i: "Microfinance works best with fair rates and training."

h: When a startup raises money at a lower value 📉
m: A funding round where the startup is valued lower than in its previous round.
e: A startup valued at Rs 500 crore last year now raises money at Rs 300 crore.
i: "Down rounds hurt morale but can save a company."

h: Free software built by thousands of strangers 🌐
m: Software whose code is public, so anyone can use, study and improve it.
e: Android and Linux are built on open-source software.
i: "Open source speeds up innovation because everyone can build on it."

h: Why your cab fare doubles when it rains ☔
m: Prices that change automatically with demand, time or supply.
e: Cab apps charge more during heavy rain or peak office hours.
i: "Dynamic pricing balances demand, but must stay fair to customers."

h: Your investments have a group name. Know it 💼
m: The full collection of investments a person or fund holds.
e: Meera's portfolio has mutual funds, a fixed deposit, some gold and two shares.
i: "I review my portfolio once a year to keep the balance right."

h: Not a fresher anymore? This is how you'll be hired 🧑‍💼
m: Hiring experienced professionals from other companies for mid-level roles.
e: A bank hires a manager with 5 years' experience from another bank.
i: "Lateral hires bring ready skills, but need time to fit the culture."

h: A bank owned by its own customers? Yes 🤝
m: A bank owned and run by its members, often for farmers or a local community.
e: Many dairy farmers in Gujarat and Maharashtra bank with local cooperative banks.
i: "Cooperative banks serve local needs that big banks may miss."

h: 1,000 people giving ₹500 can fund a dream 🙌
m: Raising small amounts of money from many people, usually online.
e: A filmmaker raises Rs 10 lakh from thousands of fans to make an independent film.
i: "Crowdfunding also tests if people actually want the product."

h: Work in small sprints, not one big launch 🏃
m: A way of working in short cycles, delivering small parts and improving with feedback.
e: A team builds an app feature in 2 weeks, shows it to users and improves it in the next sprint.
i: "Agile helps teams change direction quickly when needs change."

h: Those 'points' you collect are not free 🎟️
m: A scheme that rewards customers for buying again and again.
e: A coffee chain gives you a free drink after every 10 purchases.
i: "A good loyalty program makes coming back feel rewarding."

h: How much in shares, gold and FD? There's a plan 🥧
m: Deciding how to split money between investments like shares, bonds and gold.
e: A 25-year-old might keep 70% in equity funds, 20% in debt and 10% in gold.
i: "Asset allocation matters more than picking the 'best' share."

h: Not fired for bad work. Here's the difference 📉
m: When a company lets employees go because of cost-cutting or business changes, not their performance.
e: A tech company lays off 10% of staff after losing a big client.
i: "A layoff is a business decision, so it says little about your ability."

h: Banks must lend some money to farmers. By rule 🌱
m: An RBI rule that makes banks give a fixed share of loans to areas like agriculture and small businesses.
e: Banks must give a set share of their loans to farmers, MSMEs and education.
i: "It makes sure credit reaches sectors that need it most."

h: Talk to 50 customers before you build anything 🗣️
m: Talking to potential customers to understand their real problems before building a solution.
e: Before building a hostel app, students interview 50 hostel residents about their daily problems.
i: "Customer discovery saves months of building the wrong thing."

h: India makes billions of digital payments a month. You're one 💳
m: Paying for things using phones, cards or the internet instead of cash.
e: From paying the auto driver to buying a train ticket, most payments now happen on phones.
i: "Digital payments leave a record, which builds credit history."

h: Looked at shoes once. Now they follow you everywhere 👟
m: Showing ads to people who visited your website but did not buy.
e: You check a bag on a shopping site and later see ads for that same bag on Instagram.
i: "Retargeting reminds interested people, so it often converts better."

h: Your real wealth isn't your salary 🧮
m: Everything you own minus everything you owe.
e: Someone with Rs 10 lakh in assets and a Rs 4 lakh loan has a net worth of Rs 6 lakh.
i: "Tracking net worth yearly shows if you are truly getting richer."

h: Laid off? This payment softens the blow 💼
m: Money paid to employees when their job ends due to layoffs.
e: A company gives 3 months' salary as severance to employees it lays off.
i: "Fair severance protects a company's reputation as an employer."

h: A loan to start small, without collateral 🛠️
m: A government scheme that gives small business loans without collateral.
e: A young man takes a Mudra loan to buy a food cart and start his own business.
i: "Mudra loans help first-time entrepreneurs get started."

h: Not ready yet. Try it anyway 🧪
m: Releasing an early version of a product to a small group to test and improve it.
e: An app opens to 500 users first, fixes bugs, and then launches for everyone.
i: "A beta launch catches problems before they reach every customer."

h: A virtual world where people meet, work and shop 🥽
m: Shared online virtual spaces where people interact through digital avatars.
e: Some brands have opened virtual stores where avatars try on digital clothes.
i: "The metaverse is still early, so businesses test it carefully."

h: 10,000 views but only 2,000 people? Here's why 👀
m: The number of different people who saw your content or ad.
e: One person seeing a post five times counts as one reach but five impressions.
i: "I track reach to know how many new people we are touching."

h: When your bank lets you spend more than you have 🏧
m: A facility that lets an account holder withdraw more than their balance, up to a limit.
e: A shopkeeper uses an overdraft to buy Diwali stock and repays it after the festive sales.
i: "An overdraft helps with short gaps in cash, but interest adds up fast."
tm: Fixed loan for a set time.

h: That festive bonus has a legal side too 🪔
m: An extra payment many Indian employers give before Diwali. Many workers also have a legal right to a yearly bonus.
e: Many factories and offices pay staff a festive bonus or gifts before Diwali.
i: "A festive bonus boosts morale at the time people need extra money most."

h: Delivery partners, freelancers, drivers: the new workforce 🛵
m: An economy where many people work short-term or task-based jobs instead of permanent ones.
e: Food delivery riders and freelance designers are part of the gig economy.
i: "The gig economy gives flexibility but often lacks job security."

h: Why sweets, cars and phones sell more in Oct-Nov 🪔
m: Regular ups and downs in sales that repeat at the same time each year.
e: Car and electronics sales in India jump during Navratri and Diwali every year.
i: "We plan stock and ads around seasonality, especially the festive season."

h: Recruiters Google you. What will they find? 🔍
m: The trail of information you leave online through posts, comments and searches.
e: A recruiter checks a candidate's LinkedIn and public posts before calling for an interview.
i: "I keep my digital footprint professional, because it's my online CV."
tm: How you want to be seen.

h: Likes are nice. This number is better ❤️💬
m: The share of viewers who like, comment, share or save your content.
e: A post seen by 1,000 people that gets 50 likes and comments has 5% engagement.
i: "High engagement means the audience actually cares about the content."

h: Money isn't free. Even for big companies 💰
m: The return a company must pay to lenders and shareholders for using their money.
e: If a company borrows at 10%, any new project must earn more than that to be worth it.
i: "A project makes sense only if its return beats the cost of capital."

h: Paid just for staying? Yes, it happens 🎁
m: Extra money given to key employees to encourage them to stay.
e: During a merger, a company pays its best engineers a bonus to stay for one more year.
i: "Retention bonuses buy time, but culture keeps people for long."

h: The event nobody saw coming. And it changes everything 🦢
m: A rare, unexpected event with a huge impact on the economy or markets.
e: The COVID-19 pandemic shut down businesses worldwide almost overnight.
i: "Since black swans can't be predicted, businesses keep buffers."
